metadata.case_name: WONG SHUI MING v. YEUNG CHUN FAI AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: a sub-trochanteric fracture near the upper end of the bone
source: He was found to have sustained two fractures of the right femur, a sub-trochanteric fracture near the upper end of the bone and a second fracture of the lower end of the femur involving the knee joint.

injuries.description: a fracture of the lower end of the femur involving the knee joint
source: He was found to have sustained two fractures of the right femur, a sub-trochanteric fracture near the upper end of the bone and a second fracture of the lower end of the femur involving the knee joint.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg

injuries.description: an abscess on the upper wound (drainage operation carried out)
source: On the 2nd April 1980 a drainage operation was carried out an abscess on the upper wound and on 19th May 1981 the plate and nail were removed.
The Plaintiff has a marked osteo-arthritis of the knee.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg

manifestations.description: The Plaintiff has a marked restriction of the hip joint and cannot straighten his knee.
There is mild restriction of the ankle joint movement because of disuse of the leg.
will always need to walk with a stick and will feel pain if he has to walk a significant distance.
severe shock, several periods of severe pain, considerable worry and loss of livelihood and enjoyment of life as a result of the accident.

treatments_received: On 14 December 1979 the sub-trochanteric fracture was treated by the insertion of a nail attached to a bone plate secured to the shaft of the femur with bone screws.
On 30th October 1979 the lower fracture was operated on and two bone screws secured it in position.
On the 2nd April 1980 a drainage operation was carried out an abscess on the upper wound.
On 19th May 1981 the plate and nail were removed.
On the 12th June 1982 the screws were removed from the lower fracture site.
treatments_future: There was a chance that a further operation to fix the knee joint would be needed in the future.

losses.description: will always need to walk with a stick and will feel pain if he has to walk a significant distance.
loss of livelihood and enjoyment of life as a result of the accident; Plaintiff unable to continue caisson work and limited in ability to perform carpenter work
